Sana (AE): Hey team — Rachel at ClearBank just confirmed they want an on-prem POC in a completely isolated datacenter (no egress). They asked about packaging, how upgrades work, and whether we can support a monthly security patch cadence.

Miguel (SE): Thanks Sana. Quick checklist: installer format (tar vs signed image), bundle signing, delta updates, HSM/KMS for keys, and transport (secure USB vs courier). Do we have an existing microbundle option for tiny sites?

Tess (Product Ops): We don't have an official "microbundle" SKU, but we can trim nonessential telemetry and models to make a smaller package. Typical bundles are ~20GB; a trimmed bundle can be ~5-8GB depending on model.

Arjun (Security): For an isolated environment we require signed bundles + an integrity check step. Recommend SHA256 + detached signature. E.g.:

```
sha256sum redwood-bundle.tar.gz > redwood-bundle.sha256
openssl dgst -sha256 -sign private.key -out redwood-bundle.sig redwood-bundle.sha256
```

Miguel (SE): For upgrades, we can support quarterly full-bundle upgrades and monthly security patches as delta chunks. Deltas would be binary diffs of runtime + model weights; they require our installer to apply and verify signatures. Important: customer must agree to an offline install runbook.

Rachel (Customer): Can you clarify what the offline runbook looks like? Also, we need to know whether we can refuse telemetry permanently (no call-home).

Sana (AE): Rachel — yes, no call-home is possible in Private mode. We will provide a runbook for offline verification + optional health checks that run locally only. Miguel, can you outline the runbook steps at a high level?

Miguel (SE): High level offline runbook: 1) Receive signed bundle via courier/USB; 2) Verify SHA256 and signature on an airgapped host; 3) Import customer KMS/HSM keys or use provided PKCS#11 token; 4) Run installer in dr mode: `./install.sh --airgap --verify-signature`; 5) Smoke tests against a local test harness; 6) Approve service start.

Priya (Legal): Also flagging licensing: on-prem Dedicated license differs from Hosted. We need a signed SOW that lists support windows for patching, how many maintenance cycles are included, and any escrow terms for emergency fixes. Rachel — will your procurement team accept a time-and-materials emergency hotfix clause?

Rachel (Customer): Procurement will want a cap on emergency fees. Also asking if you can provide a vulnerability disclosure timeline (e.g., 72h patch + 30d full upgrade).

Arjun (Security): We can commit to a 72h initial mitigation advisory and aim for a 30d fix window for critical CVEs, but final SLA depends on severity and whether fix requires model/training data changes. We'll include the vuln disclosure timeline in the security questionnaire response.

Tess (Product Ops): Operational constraints: if customer chooses monthly security deltas, we need a signed delta manifest for each patch and a rolling rollback artifact. Deltas are atomic but we only support one rollback step (previous good bundle), so customers should schedule maintenance windows. Also, delta delivery requires us to ship a manifest and signed checkpoint file.

Miguel (SE): One more technical constraint: KV cache format and model quantization must be compatible across delta updates. If the customer wants to switch quantization (e.g., int8 -> int4) we treat that as a major upgrade and it will be a full bundle, not a delta.

Rachel (Customer): Understood. For logistics: we have an internal security team that will want bundle provenance, SBOM for runtime libs, and a reproducible build statement. Can you provide SBOM and build hashes?

Sana (AE): Yes — we can provide SBOM, build hashes, and a signed attest file. Miguel/Tess — what is the typical lead time to generate SBOM + attestation for a POC bundle?

Tess (Product Ops): SBOM + attestation generation is automated but needs a build run. If we use an existing curated model + runtime, lead time is 2 business days. If we need to custom-quantize or prune a model, add 3-5 business days for QC.

Miguel (SE): Deployment question: does customer plan to use an HSM for key storage or a software-keystore? HSM integration requires PKCS#11 support and we need to pre-test on their HSM model.

Rachel (Customer): We have Thales Luna HSMs. We'll coordinate a test unit for validation.

Arjun (Security): Good — send HSM vendor + firmware version. We'll validate PKCS#11 compatibility and provide any required middleware notes. Also we'll supply the security questionnaire answers (redacted PII) in a separate artifact.

Sana (AE): Action items: 1) Miguel/Tess: prepare a trimmed POC microbundle (target 6GB) + SBOM + attestation; 2) Arjun: draft security questionnaire answers + vuln disclosure SLA note; 3) Priya: prepare SOW template with emergency cap language; 4) Rachel: share HSM model + procurement constraints.

Miguel (SE): I'll start the microbundle build now and loop in infra if we need special quantization passes. ETA for initial artifacts: 3 business days.

deploy-bot: scheduled artifact-generation-job started for bundle id=pbx-1716009876, status=running

Rachel (Customer): Thanks — that timeline works. Can we plan a dry-run install with your SEs the week after artifacts are ready?

Sana (AE): Yes — let's tentatively book a 90min dry run. I'll follow up with calendar options once Miguel confirms build completion. :thumbsup:
